svg.text: Top: one sharp peak near 11 years, the Schwabe cycle, computed from nothing but the numbers (the orange band is the mean cycle length from the minima, 11.04 ± 1.18 years).
Its shoulders (about 10 and 12 years) come from the cycles' changing length and strength; the bump near 100 years is the Gleissberg modulation. Bottom: flip the sign of every
other cycle, as the Sun's magnetic field flips, and the peak moves to about 22 years: the Hale cycle. Counting spots throws the polarity away, like a rectifier, and doubles the
